subject: Nimbus launch: dedicated reserve + short-term burst planning
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@nimbus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Henry Chen <henry@ops.nimbus.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@nimbus.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Launch spike planning — request for burst allowance

Hi Soojin,

Quick context: Nimbus is launching a targeted promotion on 2026-08-05 (US daytime) that we expect will spike traffic for our assistant feature. Our internal projection (attached) shows baseline inference at ~120 qps and short peak windows reaching 1,200 qps for roughly 45–90 minutes. Token lengths average 80 tokens per request; about 35% of requests hit tool-calls.

We currently have a Dedicated capacity agreement in discussion (deal RNW-2026-0789) and want to make sure the Dedicated environment can handle the launch without impacting latency. Specifically we are asking:
- Can Redwood provide a short-term burst allowance (3–4x baseline) for one 2-hour window on 2026-08-05?
- What autoscaling policy and pre-warm steps would you recommend to avoid cold-start latency?
- Ballpark incremental cost for that burst window vs. a month of extra reserved capacity?

Attached: nimbus-launch-traffic-projections.csv

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful — our engineering/ops team (cc: Henry) is available this week.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Nimbus Systems
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike planning — request for burst allowance

Maya — thanks for the projection and the heads up. This is the right time to plan so we can avoid surprises on the day of. High level answers first, then a proposed next step and attachments.

Summary (quick):
- We can support a 3x baseline burst for a 2-hour window on 2026-08-05 using a combination of reserved GPUs + temporary burst pool.
- Recommended autoscale: reserved capacity handles baseline, warm pool of pre-allocated GPUs (15–20% of peak) + immediate burst from a transient pool (up to 3x baseline) with model-fallback enabled.
- Pre-warm: schedule warm pool to start 45–60 minutes before the window; run synthetic prompts to populate KV cache and embeddings so first-user requests see production latency.
- Cost: approximate incremental cost for the single 2-hr burst looks like ~0.6–0.9x of one additional reserved GPU-month (we'll provide exact numbers after you confirm GPU type and acceptable fallback model).

Questions I need to finalize numbers:
1) Are you expecting the full 1,200 qps to be evenly distributed across regions or concentrated in US-west?
2) Can you confirm the average prompt length is 80 tokens (as in file) and the heavy tail percentage for >256 tokens?
3) Which latency SLO matters most: p50/p90/p99? We typically optimize for p90 <= 200ms for interactive apps.

Attached: proposed-burst-schedule-v1.xlsx, dedicated-burst-runbook.txt

Next step: Connor (cc'd) will run a rapid sizing sketch (GPU counts + warm pool sizes) once you confirm Q1–Q3 above. I can also draft a short amendment to the Dedicated contract for the single-event burst allowance (commercial credit / capped overage) and route it to Vivek for signoff.

If helpful I can set a 30-min call today or tomorrow — let me know what works.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@nimbus.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike planning — request for burst allowance

On Mon, Jul 13, 2026 at 11:04 -0700, Soojin Lee wrote:
> Maya — thanks for the projection and the heads up. This is the right time to plan so we can avoid surprises on the day of.

Adding technical sizing details and a couple of pragmatic fallbacks. Below are conservative estimates — we can tighten them when you confirm token distribution and percent of tool-calls that trigger external services.

Assumptions (for the sketch):
- Model: 13B decoder-only (your current baseline).
- Avg tokens: 80 in, 80 out.
- Baseline qps: 120 -> peak 1,200 qps.
- Target p90 latency: <= 250ms (interactive).

Sizing sketch (rough):
- Reserved pool (handles baseline + buffer): 8 x H100-80GB equiv GPUs (handles ~150 qps sustained each depending on batch/quantization).
- Warm pool (pre-warmed, kept idle until T-60m): 4 x H100-80GB equiv. Warm pool is online at t=-60m and runs synthetic workloads to populate KV cache and tiled embeddings.
- Burst transient pool: ability to add 18 x H100-80GB equiv for egress to reach ~3x baseline for a 2-hr window. These are ephemeral nodes that can be allocated from our shared burst fabric or from short-term reserved capacity (customer choice).

Operational notes:
- Cold-start delta: full node startup + model load can be 3–5 minutes for H100; KV cache warm adds another 2–3 minutes unless we pre-warm. That is why we recommend t=-60m pre-warm.
- Continuous batching: During the peak we enable aggressive batching with adaptive timeouts. This reduces per-token cost but can increase p99; we keep a small latency-protect ring (dedicated low-latency workers) to serve critical low-latency traffic.
- Fallback model: If burst capacity cannot provision fast enough, automatic fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant with similar output fidelity reduces compute by ~2.5x with minimal regression for most prompts. We can enable this as a controlled policy.

Attachments: gpu-sizing-notes.md (contains per-GPU qps table), latency-estimates.csv (p50/p90/p99 sketches across configurations).

Operational checklist (short):
- Confirm region distribution (we found multi-region splits add ~10–15% extra capacity need).
- Authorize warm-pool start window and confirm synthetic prompts corpus to pre-warm.
- Decide whether burst pool should come from Redwood shared fabric (faster but metered) vs short-term reserved (slower to provision but predictable cost).

Happy to run a quick basic simulation if you share a small sample of request logs (anonymized).

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@nimbus.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbus.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike planning — request for burst allowance

Maya — looping in commercial/legal fyi and to propose the commercial guardrails.

Thanks for initiating this. We can accommodate the single-event burst as discussed, and propose the following commercial terms for the amendment to your Dedicated contract:
1) One-time burst allowance: up to 3x baseline for a single 2-hour window on 2026-08-05.
2) Cap on incremental charges for the event: no more than the cost of one additional reserved GPU-month (customer pays any excess beyond that cap).
3) Pre-warm and runbook: Redwood will execute the pre-warm steps (t=-60m) and run the provided synthetic prompts as part of the service.
4) SLA exception note: during a burst window we will make every effort to maintain p90 latency targets but will include an explicit burst window clause that relaxes p99 guarantees by up to 50ms.

Action items:
- Maya: confirm region split and approve warm-pool start time.
- Procurement: if acceptable we'll send an amendment + DocuSign link (HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654321).
- Redwood ops: Connor, please prepare final GPU counts and the short implementation runbook.

If procurement prefers credits instead of a capped charge, we're open — suggest a one-time credit equal to 0.75x reserved GPU-month; print in the amendment and sign.

I'll draft and route the amendment today once we get Maya's confirm.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
